title: Quantifying the safety benefit of generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) loops for multi‑vendor network‑configuration generation (adapter‑aligned preregistration)
research_question: To what extent does a deterministic-validated generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increase the proportion of non‑harmful, validator‑passing vendor-specific configurations produced from operator intent, compared to direct LLM generation without validation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (confirmatory): Per task (paired design, n=300), the G‑V‑R pipeline yields a higher paired probability of 'task success' than direct LLM generation, where a task is a success if the validator accepts the candidate produced by the baseline initial generation (baseline) versus the guarded arm where the same initial candidate is validated and, if it fails, a single deterministic-repair generation is attempted (guarded). The primary test compares per-task paired binary outcomes (success_guarded minus success_baseline).
exploratory_questions: E1: Conditional on initial validator failure, what fraction of single automatic repairs succeed (repair success rate) and which validator violation types are most repairable under one repair attempt?
E2: Per‑vendor differences in baseline and G‑V‑R improvement (Cisco IOS vs JunOS vs Arista).

E3: Relationship between model‑call budget consumed (one initial generation + optional one repair per task) and marginal increase in per‑task success (diminishing returns within the one-repair policy).
benchmark_scope: Curated public 300-task multi-vendor NetOps intent manifest (Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista). Tasks limited to vendor CLI fragments expressing configuration-change intents; manifest published with provenance tags and deterministic hashes.

Deterministic validator rule set (published): syntactic correctness, interface assignment invariants, basic routing reachability invariants, and ACL/route-policy destructive-pattern detection. Validator rules, canonicalization, and parser code are published with the study Docker image.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (difference in per-task probability that the guarded arm yields a validator-pass vs the baseline arm, paired across tasks)
sampling_plan: Paired tasks n = 300. For each task: (1) produce one initial candidate configuration using the preregistered vendor prompt (this single initial candidate is shared between conditions); (2) Baseline arm outcome: success if initial candidate passes deterministic validator (no additional model calls). (3) Guarded arm outcome: validate the same initial candidate; if it passes → success; if it fails → issue a single automatic repair LLM call (one repair) and re-validate repaired candidate; guarded success if repaired candidate passes. Per-task binary outcome defined as success if the arm produced a validator-pass within the allowed per-task model-call budget (baseline ≤1 call; guarded ≤2 calls). Inclusion: tasks from the published manifest; exclude only tasks whose intent deterministically fails parsing prior to generation (hash-signed and logged). Stopping rule: execute all 300 tasks once (no interim stopping). Pre-registered RNG: one seed per task for deterministic metadata; seeds recorded in execution manifest. All raw outputs, logs, and hashes stored and published.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: detect absolute increase of 10 percentage points (0.10) in per-task success probability with two-sided alpha=0.05 and power≈0.80. Clustering unit: task (n_pairs = 300). Calculation method: paired-proportions (McNemar-style) guidance under reasonable discordance assumptions; sensitivity curves and exact power given observed baseline discordance will be reported. Sensitivity analyses include baseline rates 0.30 and 0.50 and up to 10% pair censoring.
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks whose operator-intent manifest entry cannot be deterministically parsed into the adapter's task format prior to any model call (logged, hash-signed).
Auto-exclude individual samples containing disallowed sensitive tokens or parser failures (logged).
missingness_plan: Follow preregistered retry policy for transient model-call failures (deterministic retry attempts per call recorded). If after retries a sample call is unrecoverable, mark that sample 'failed-call'. Confirmatory analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (pairs retained; if both arms have only failed calls the pair is counted as paired failure). Sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats failed-call samples as failing. All missingness logs are hash-signed and published.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Inputs: paired binary outcomes per task (success_baseline, success_guarded). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: two-sided McNemar-style paired binary test with 95% Wilson-style CI reported. Failed-call treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' (primary) and sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Secondary analyses: per-vendor paired binary tests with Bonferroni correction (family alpha=0.05 -> per-comparison alpha≈0.0167). Exploratory outputs: repair success conditional on initial failure (proportion), violation-type frequencies, and descriptive model-call counts. All analysis code, raw inputs, and outputs will be published and hash-signed.
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis: single overall paired test. Three pre-specified secondary per-vendor paired comparisons corrected with Bonferroni (alpha_family=0.05 -> per-comparison alpha≈0.0167). All other analyses are exploratory and labeled as such.
